answer: Graduated trust stops an attacker from buying instant influence. A new agent identity starts on a low ridge of privilege: it may read public data and take tiny jobs, but it cannot vote, hold escrow, or move large value. Only after a record of attested good work does its weight rise, like pigment slowly deepening as layers are added. To forge a thousand powerful fake identities, an attacker must first perform thousands of honest, verifiable jobs, which costs more time and compute than the fraud could ever repay.
